items.title: 'Systemic racism' claims tip of the iceberg in buried reef authority review
items.description: The damning results of a review into the agency tasked with managing the Great Barrier Reef, an area bigger than New Zealand and home to 70 traditional owner groups, has never before seen the light of day.

items.title: Concerns hospital giant could 'cherrypick' private patients from public hospital
items.description: A trial to ease pressure on a public emergency department has raised concerns a multi-million-dollar company is getting a special deal.

items.title: AI giants on the nose: Why those stellar super earnings are under threat
items.description: Overshadowing the tumult that is global politics has been a financial boom beyond almost anything witnessed before, focused entirely on the perceived benefits wrought by a brave new world of AI that threatens to up-end our lives.

items.title: The AFL's dilemma: How to protect players without changing the game
items.description: Contact is an essential part of footy, but there is growing evidence it can also be a grave threat to the health and welfare of its players. Experts say the AFL should be acting now to protect current and future players.

items.title: Giveaway club RS Rewards accused of 'ongoing and misleading conduct'
items.description: One of Australia's biggest "rewards clubs" has been banned from running any gaming activity in New South Wales for 18 months after allegedly breaking the law.

items.title: Live: Brazil breaks Japan hearts with last-minute winner
items.description: Brazil's Gabriel Martinelli scores in the 96th minute to break Japan's hearts and secure a 2-1 round of 32 win for the Seleção.

items.title: ABC presenter Trevor Chappell to hang up mic after 26 years
items.description: After decades of keeping night owls and shift workers company on ABC radio across Australia, Overnights presenter Trevor Chappell decides to call it a day at the age of 65.

items.title: Social media giants face fines for failing to hand over documents
items.description: Labor wants to double the fines for tech giants who refuse to hand over documents that could prove they are failing to enforce Australia’s social media age ban.

items.title: 'Had to do something': As auction clearance rates drop PM defends policy
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese issues an impassioned defence of CGT changes from the budget and Australia's multicultural society.

items.title: Government vows crackdown on sale of NDIS shell companies
items.description: The federal government says it is moving to crack down on the growing trade in "off-the-shelf" NDIS providers.

items.title: Most Australians have never heard of this medicine-safety program
items.description: A little black triangle on medicine information leaflets is meant to make it easier to report adverse effects of new medications. Problem is, many Australians don't know what it means.

items.title: PM-in-waiting Andy Burnham lays out plan to fix 'broken' British politics
items.description: Andy Burnham, the British MP tipped to replace the outgoing prime minister Sir Keir Starmer, promised "radical change" to the nation's "broken" political system as he laid out his vision to lead the country on Monday.

items.title: Court rejects Trump's final bid to overturn E. Jean Carroll verdict
items.description: The US Supreme Court declined to hear US President Donald Trump's bid to overturn a $5 million USD verdict in a case in which a jury found him liable for sexually abusing and defaming E Jean Carroll.

items.title: Six killed in German 'family tragedy' shooting, say police
items.description: Two people have been arrested after a shooting in the northern German town of Stade.

items.title: BalletTok, blackface and nudes: Inside the world of professional ballet
items.description: Ariane Beeston, the author of an acclaimed memoir detailing her experience with postpartum psychosis, has penned her first work of fiction, Don't Forget to Smile.

items.title: Doing your own tax return? Watch out for these common mistakes
items.description: With side hustles, working from home, crypto investments, renting out rooms and receiving income through digital platforms or apps, experts say people are at greater risk of making errors with their tax.

items.title: Quiz: Will you raise the white flag on these tricky flag questions?
items.description: How many stars are there on the US flag? And how many stars are on the Europe flag?

items.title: Bondi terror attack survivor received 'influx of hate' hours after shooting
items.description: Deepfake and altered images depicting a Bondi Beach terror attack survivor holding an Academy Award while covered in blood spread "like wildfire" online just hours after the shooting, a royal commission has heard.

items.title: Putin says Russia will press on despite fuel shortages
items.description: President Vladimir Putin has said Russia will press ahead with its battlefield aim of fully capturing four Ukrainian regions, rejecting diplomatic overtures from Ukraine.

items.title: Penelope Keith, star of 'The Good Life' and 'To the Manor Born', dead at 86
items.description: Beloved British actress Dame Penelope Keith, who rose to fame in the hit 1970s UK sitcom "The Good Life", has died aged 86.

items.title: Sam Kerr returns to the United States after Chelsea exit
items.description: Matilda's striker Sam Kerr has returned to the United States following her successful stint at London giants, Chelsea.

items.title: The lucrative business of super switching is ringing alarm bells
items.description: There is now more than $1 trillion in self-managed superannuation funds, which means a big chunk of money isn't regulated by APRA, and it's the rate of the shift into SMSFs and less-regulated managed investment schemes that has regulators worried.

items.title: Closure of long-term residential facility run by Salvos sparks concerns
items.description: A long-term residential facility in Melbourne's inner-west will begin the process of shutting down, raising concerns about the future of dozens of vulnerable men.

items.title: Vanuatu critical infrastructure to remain 'free from militarisation' under pact
items.description: Vanuatu's Prime Minister Jotham Napat and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ink the Nakamal Agreement, almost 10 months after Mr Napat pulled out of a planned signing ceremony in Port Vila, citing concerns around sovereignty.

items.title: Court finds staffer's relationship with 20yo parolee 'grossly inappropriate'
items.description: An Alice Springs parole worker found in a hotel room with the 20-year-old she was responsible for supporting has avoided prison for attempting to pervert the course of justice.
